summary.headline: TII Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 18% to Rs 2,366 Cr, but PBT fell to Rs 213 Cr on steel cost lag; management expects full recovery.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue grew to Rs 2,366 Cr from Rs 2,007 Cr, while standalone PBT declined to Rs 213 Cr from Rs 222 Cr, with management attributing margin pressure to steel price increases in Q4 and Q1 that pass through to customers with a 2-3 quarter lag. Engineering revenue rose 21% to Rs 1,566 Cr with flat PBIT at Rs 153 Cr, and Metal Formed Products PBIT fell to Rs 28 Cr from Rs 37 Cr despite 11.5% revenue growth. The e-mobility (Clean Mobility) business posted its highest-ever quarterly turnover of close to Rs 240 Cr and management said losses likely peaked, with volumes up about 64% QoQ. Management said steel price recovery, including Q1 under-recovery, will be fully recovered, while non-steel inflation (fuel, freight) recovery talks with OEMs are ongoing.

segments.name: Engineering
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,566 Cr vs Rs 1,298 Cr YoY; PBIT flat at Rs 153 Cr. Volume grew about 17%, and margins were hit by steel cost inflation.

segments.name: Metal Formed Products (MFP)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 408 Cr vs Rs 366 Cr YoY (about 11.5%), but PBIT fell to Rs 28 Cr from Rs 37 Cr. Growth was volume-led, with railways a drag and a Hyundai-linked unit weak; a western region greenfield plant is delayed by six months.

segments.name: Mobility (Clean Mobility / e-mobility)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 250 Cr vs Rs 198 Cr YoY; PBIT Rs 9 Cr vs Rs 7 Cr. Management cited highest-ever turnover of close to Rs 240 Cr (the call figure), with negative EBIT narrowing by about Rs 40-50 Cr per analyst, and three-wheeler billing of 1,924 units.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 256 Cr vs Rs 236 Cr YoY; PBIT Rs 21 Cr vs Rs 17 Cr. Includes TI Medical, CDMO (3xper) and Orange Koi, the newly acquired metal injection moulding start-up.

guidance_outlook: Management expects steel price increases, including the Q1 under-recovery, to be fully recovered with a lag, with margin neutralisation in coming quarters.
Management declined to quantify the Q1 under-recovery but reiterated guidance for double-digit EBIT margin growth.
Non-steel inflation (fuel, freight) recovery under discussion with OEMs; update expected in about one quarter.
Cycles business: management targets about 2 bps (as stated, likely 2 percentage points) further margin improvement for FY27 to reach about 5% margin.
TI Medical core surgical business expected to grow about 20% YoY with profitability; IV cannula acquisition plant to start revenue from August/September 2026.
Jayem expected to add a battery business stream; one EV business expected to break even in FY27, and two more in FY28.
Rs 750 Cr total capital infusion into new ventures over time; Rs 250 Cr infused in Q4 FY26, another Rs 250 Cr expected in Q3 FY27.
Management expects engineering demand to remain bullish for the next one or two quarters, barring geopolitical disruption.
capex_capacity: TI standalone capex planned at about Rs 350 Cr for FY27; Shanthi Gears about Rs 100 Cr; group ex-CG Power about Rs 600-700 Cr, per CFO.
Capex directed to engineering and MFP divisions, plus TI Medical and 3xper CDMO.
3xper CDMO 200 KL intermediate capacity: commissioning done, validation batches underway, clean room commissioning in 30-40 days, customer PAS filing and inspection expected in FY28.
Greenfield MFP plant in western region delayed by six months.
Clean Mobility: L3 autos introduced in select UP and Bihar markets on a test basis; tipper (28-ton) sold about 20-25 units, with market shifting to 35-ton and above.
demand_pricing: Engineering volume grew about 17% in Q1; management said exports grew strongly with double-digit growth; exports are about 14% of TI revenue.
Steel price increases in Q4 and Q1 caused margin compression; pass-through lag of 2-3 quarters.
Cycles business benefited from strong Q1 seasonality (schools and colleges reopening) with higher market share.
Clean Mobility billing volumes in Q1: 86 heavy trucks, 1,924 three-wheelers, 347 small commercial vehicles, 22 tractors. Three-wheeler FY26 billing about 6,700 vs Vahan registrations about 6,500.
Cell prices expected to stay firm through at least Q3 FY27 due to BESS demand; mitigation via pre-booking long lead-time orders.
Nepal: about 100+ three-wheeler units shipped or in process; African markets (Tanzania, Ethiopia) at exploratory stage.
HCV deployments: about 22 trucks at Welspun's Anjar port, plus single-digit deployments at Vizag and Chennai ports, and Wonder Cement at Tuna and Dahej ports.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further price hikes from customers to offset steel-driven margin compression in Engineering and MFP, or is Q1 profitability the underlying run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said steel increases from Q4 and Q1 are recovered with a 2-3 quarter lag and expects margin neutralisation in coming quarters; it declined to quantify the Q1 under-recovery but reiterated double-digit EBIT margin growth guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the steel under-recovery be recovered cumulatively, not just passed through with lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed: steel price increases including Q1 will be fully recovered.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in MFP to drive 11.5% revenue growth, given railways was a drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was volume-led with no price recovery yet; railways remained a drag and the Hyundai-dependent unit was weak, while a western region greenfield plant is delayed by six months.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly Rs 40-50 Cr reduction in e-mobility negative EBIT, and is this one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Clean Mobility posted its highest-ever turnover of close to Rs 240 Cr with traction across all four businesses; volumes rose about 64% QoQ. Management confirmed it is routine volume-driven, not a one-off benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Are e-mobility losses past peak and what are breakeven timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Directionally yes, losses are past peak if volumes keep rising QoQ; one business expected to break even this year and two more in the next financial year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is three-wheeler billing (1,924 in Q1) above Vahan registrations?
qa_highlights.answer: Billing-to-registration lag of 30-45 days; FY26 billing was about 6,700 vs Vahan about 6,500, and Q4 billing was only about 1,200 due to a supply-link issue. Numbers tend to tally within 3-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: How much standalone capital will be infused into new ventures in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 250 Cr infused in Q4 FY26 and another Rs 250 Cr expected in Q3 FY27, within an overall Rs 750 Cr guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How will non-steel inflation (fuel, freight) from the West Asia crisis be recovered, and when will margins normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Discussions with OEMs on non-steel recovery have started; an update is expected in about a quarter, and management is hopeful most of it will be recovered.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the cycles margin expansion and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Strong Q1 seasonality (schools and colleges reopening) and higher market share; management targets about 2 more basis points (likely percentage points) of improvement, with about 5% margin as the current target.

qa_highlights.question: What is Orange Koi, and what is the plan?
qa_highlights.answer: A small metal injection moulding start-up acquired as a step into additive manufacturing; it sits in Others, with a strategy update expected in about two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jayem outlook, and are its batteries for captive use?
qa_highlights.answer: Jayem faced design and development headwinds; a battery assembly line is being set up as a third revenue stream, initially for in-house SCV and three-wheeler use, with external sales later.

qa_highlights.question: What are group capex plans excluding CG Power?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 350 Cr for TI standalone and Rs 100 Cr for Shanthi Gears in FY27, with group ex-CG Power around Rs 600-700 Cr; spend goes to Engineering, MFP, TI Medical and 3xper CDMO.

qa_highlights.question: What is the structure and timing of external investors in TI Clean Mobility?
qa_highlights.answer: Three external investors hold CCPS that convert only at IPO, with no fixed timeline; stake will be set by valuation at that time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demand outlook and export share for Engineering?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand expected to stay bullish for one or two quarters barring geopolitical disruption; exports grew at double-digit rates and are about 14% of TI revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cell supply and price outlook for Clean Mobility?
qa_highlights.answer: Cell prices expected to stay firm at least through Q3 FY27 due to BESS demand; mitigation via pre-booking long lead-time orders and locking prices.

risks_watch: Recovery of steel under-recovery: timing (2-3 quarter lag) and magnitude undisclosed; management declined to quantify Q1 under-recovery.
Non-steel inflation (fuel, freight, West Asia-linked) recovery from OEMs unresolved; update due in about one quarter.
MFP: railways drag, Hyundai-linked unit weak, western greenfield plant delayed six months; volume-led growth with no price recovery yet.
Clean Mobility: sustainability of QoQ volume growth; three-wheeler billing versus Vahan registration gap; cell price firmness through Q3 FY27; tipper market shift to 35-ton plus.
TI Medical acquisition (Medicura/IV cannula) may take time on customer acquisition and margins; 3xper CDMO inspection expected in FY28.
Second Rs 250 Cr standalone infusion into new ventures due Q3 FY27; Orange Koi and Jayem profitability yet to be shown.
key_quotes: So we are confident on the steel price increase particularly. We will be able to recover fully and you will see the margin neutralization will happen in the coming quarters.
So Joseph, maybe I would not like to give particular number.
Yes, that assumption is right. For steel prices particularly, including Q1, we will be able to recover fully.

summary.management_tone: Confident on steel price recovery and volume momentum in Engineering and e-mobility, but guarded on quantification: management declined to size the Q1 under-recovery and gave no timeline for non-steel inflation recovery. Responses on CDMO, Jayem and IPO timing were hedged as timing-dependent.
